Source #1: Boutique Label USA Blu-ray (video, stereo audio, subtitles, chapters) - thanks A!
Source #2: Major Studio USA Blu-ray (surround audio, commentary, subtitles) - thanks B!
Source #3: R2 PAL DVD (subtitles) - thanks anonymous!
Source #4: Amazon, iTunes WEB-DLs (subtitles)

Video
The new 4K restoration is much more detailed than the old master and has a much brighter and more saturated grade.

Video comparison: Studio BD vs. Boutique BD

Audio
The boutique BD is the only release that includes the original stereo mix: the stereo track on the DVD is a downmix of the 5.1 surround remix. This new stereo track was transferred from the mag master and sounds great. The label was heavy-handed with their band filter on the 5.1 mix, unlike their new transfer of the stereo mix, so I used the older 5.1 track from the studio disc. This track is a bit boosted vs. the boutique disc but it doesn't have any clipping or limiting.

The commentary track was originally recorded and mixed for the old DVD. While the commentary recording itself was probably done in mono, the track was most likely mixed in stereo. A dual mono check on both of the DVD and studio BD commentary tracks shows a decent amount of stereo info.

Audio comparison: stereo, 5.1 surround, commentary

Subtitles + Chapters
English (US / SDH / main film and commentary) subtitles OCR'd, spellchecked, included in SDH and non-SDH versions, and demuxed from source 1. The SDH subtitles were manually stripped with extra care to ensure that no diegetic music cue subtitles were removed. Dutch subtitles OCR'd, spellchecked, and synced from source 3. Named chapters from source 1 adjusted to nearest I- or P-frames where necessary; end credits chapter added.

Special thanks to A for providing the source early.
